title: Build an enforceable engagement envelope
description: Choose a defensive hypothesis, then add the safeguards required to authorize its smallest useful test.

safeguards.label: Signed authorization
safeguards.detail: Approver, plan version, operators, purpose, and expiry are recorded.

safeguards.label: Named scope and exclusions
safeguards.detail: Assets, tenants, identities, data classes, and third parties are explicit.

safeguards.label: Bounded time window
safeguards.detail: Start, expiry, time zone, and any maintenance or blackout periods are defined.

safeguards.label: White-cell control
safeguards.detail: A reachable controller can identify, pause, or stop the exercise.

safeguards.label: Measurable stop conditions
safeguards.detail: Availability, scope, data, safety, and real-incident thresholds are testable.

safeguards.label: Evidence handling
safeguards.detail: Exercise IDs, storage, access, sanitization, retention, and deletion are defined.

safeguards.label: Recovery and cleanup owner
safeguards.detail: A named owner can remove artifacts, restore state, and confirm stability.

safeguards.label: Privacy and legal review
safeguards.detail: The approved proof avoids unnecessary access to personal or regulated data.

scenarios.label: Identity response hypothesis
scenarios.hypothesis: A bounded synthetic sign-in anomaly is detected, owned, and contained without locking unrelated users.
scenarios.target: Named test identities in the production identity tenant
scenarios.exclusions: Privileged break-glass accounts, customer identities, and third-party tenants
scenarios.risk: Account lockout or an incident responder containing a real user
scenarios.stopCondition: Stop on any non-test identity impact or loss of white-cell contact.
scenarios.evidenceLimit: Use synthetic identities and retain event metadata, not credential material.
scenarios.recoveryOwner: Identity platform owner restores accounts and verifies policy state.

scenarios.label: Segmentation response hypothesis
scenarios.hypothesis: A permitted traversal attempt between two test zones is denied or creates an owned investigation.
scenarios.target: Two named test workloads and one approved network path
scenarios.exclusions: Shared control planes, safety systems, and unmanaged partner networks
scenarios.risk: Unexpected load, route change, or defensive isolation of shared infrastructure
scenarios.stopCondition: Stop on route instability, shared service impact, or a target mismatch.
scenarios.evidenceLimit: Preserve flow, policy, alert, and case identifiers without copying workload data.
scenarios.recoveryOwner: Network service owner confirms routes, policies, and workload health.

scenarios.label: Response recovery hypothesis
scenarios.hypothesis: Responders can identify, isolate, and restore a designated test workload inside the recovery objective.
scenarios.target: One disposable workload with an approved restoration snapshot
scenarios.exclusions: Production data stores, shared queues, and customer-facing dependencies
scenarios.risk: Isolation or rollback propagates beyond the disposable workload
scenarios.stopCondition: Stop if isolation touches a dependency or the snapshot cannot be verified.
scenarios.evidenceLimit: Record orchestration, case, isolation, and restore events using the exercise ID.
scenarios.recoveryOwner: Service owner validates data integrity and returns the workload to its prior state.
